lines.text: You are never going to make another close friend, ever again.
Hear me out.
A professor in Kansas actually counted.
Fifty hours to get to casual.
Around ninety, and you'd call the person a friend.
Two hundred, before they're the one you call from the hospital.
Now think about where you got your friends.
School.
You didn't pick those people.
Six hours a day, for years, whether you liked it or not.
That's your two hundred hours.
The building did it for you.
Then you graduate, and suddenly friendship is an appointment.
Dinner.
Once a month, if everyone's free.
Two hours, maybe.
I did the math.
It's the kind of thing I do.
Eight years.
You could fix that.
Two hundred hours, on purpose, with one person.
Nobody's stopping you.
You are too lazy to put in the effort to make a friend.
